method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting' (last updated September 2025). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at RCH Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2 (rch.org.au)). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the Wave 1 hand-written edition (verbatim quotes) as paraphrase against the page fetched 2026-09-24. Every clinical claim of edition 1.0 is carried over; the two bibliographic claims (last-updated date, AMH Children's Dosing Companion in the reference list) now sit in the source date and a banner.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Green (bilious) vomit means gut obstruction until shown otherwise** → refer to surgeons urgently.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No diarrhoea? Look beyond gastroenteritis** for another cause of the vomiting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Always think intracranial:** raised intracranial pressure (ICP) and inflicted injury are both on the list.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ondansetron may be used to relieve symptoms, but a child who stops vomiting may still have a serious cause.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Vomiting is a symptom — common and non-specific — rather than a diagnosis.** Acute vomiting is most often caused by infection.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bile looks dark green, not yellow.** Showing families a colour chart or picture helps them describe the vomit accurately.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Headache with vomiting early in the morning can signal raised ICP.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **What the vomit looks like:** dark green (bilious) → GIT obstruction · blood → swallowed blood (e.g. a nosebleed, or in a newborn maternal blood from delivery or nipple trauma) · projectile → pyloric stenosis · early in the morning → raised ICP.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Respiratory and abdominal clues:** wheeze, stridor, rash, cough or chest pain (think anaphylaxis, viral illness, pneumonia); a distended, tender abdomen with 'tinkling' or absent bowel sounds (think obstruction); a tender abdomen with fever (think appendicitis or UTI).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pain in the lower abdomen, pelvis or testis → consider torsion** of the testis or ovary.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Gut clues:** vomiting tied to particular foods suggests non-IgE-mediated food allergy; rectal bleeding widens the list to include intussusception.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Infective and neurological clues:** fever or a systemically unwell child raises meningitis among the causes; a head injury or concern about non-accidental injury raises intracranial bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Metabolic and toxic clues:** abdominal pain with polyuria and polydipsia (DKA); a toxidrome, possible toxin ingestion or drug use (including cannabis hyperemesis); in a neonate or infant, think of inborn errors of metabolism.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Other patterns:** a recognisable recurring pattern (cyclical vomiting syndrome); urinary frequency, bodily changes or sexual activity (pregnancy); self-induced vomiting, purging or disordered eating (eating disorders).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Abdomen:** distension may point to an acute abdomen or bowel obstruction — ask the parent whether the belly looks different; high-pitched 'tinkling' or absent bowel sounds suggest obstruction. ⚠️ **Check the testes for torsion, above all in adolescent boys.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Neurology:** an altered conscious state or abnormal neurological signs (such as Cushing's triad) may mean intracranial pathology; in infants a bulging fontanelle can indicate raised ICP.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags:** bilious vomit · lethargy or listlessness · an infant who cannot be settled, with or without a bulging fontanelle · fever with neck stiffness and photophobia in an older child · peritonism · ongoing vomiting with poor growth or abnormal development.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A well child who is only vomiting usually needs no further tests;** when tests are done, pick them from the likely differentials.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Check ketones along with the BGL when the BGL is below 3 mmol/L or above 11 mmol/L.** Vomiting can lead to ketotic hypoglycaemia, especially in younger children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Shock → sodium chloride 0.9% bolus, 10-20 mL/kg.** BGL under 2.6 mmol/L → manage as hypoglycaemia. Ketones present → think about giving carbohydrate to correct them (apple juice, for example).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Involve the local surgeons when a surgical cause appears likely** — bowel obstruction, torsion of the testis or ovary, or appendicitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Purpose: helping children older than 6 months keep up their hydration.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suggested starting dose by weight:** 2 mg for 8-15 kg; 4 mg for 15-30 kg; 8 mg above 30 kg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Usable when vomiting follows a head injury,** as long as conscious state and the other signs are watched closely.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If ondansetron does not work, get senior advice before any other antiemetic,** because of their side effects.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Start with oral fluids:** oral rehydration solution, or apple juice diluted half-and-half with water (1:1).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Consider calling the local paediatric team** for advice on escalating care, for an acutely sick child whom fluid resuscitation is not improving, for severe metabolic derangement, or when the diagnosis is uncertain.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Send home when** the child is alert, keeping down small amounts orally and has normal vital signs, **and either** the cause has been found and dealt with, **or** ⚠️ high-risk diagnoses have been thought through and a follow-up plan is in place with clear advice on when to come back sooner.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Vomiting', last updated September 2025, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vomiting/, retrieved 2026-09-24
